title: Peer Review Penalizes Novel Grant Proposals
bottleneck: Grant reviewers, who are typically competitors of applicants, systematically favor safe, incremental proposals with extensive preliminary data over bold ideas. Documented cases — from prion research to mRNA work by Katalin Karikó — show Nobel-level breakthroughs initially denied funding, suggesting the system filters against exactly the work that matters most. High-risk programs remain a small fraction of agency budgets, and their evaluation criteria often drift back toward conventional metrics.
why_it_blocks: If funding selects for consensus science, transformative ideas starve at the proposal stage and progress slows to the pace of the already-agreed.
current_state: The pattern is long documented but unreformed; agencies have piloted high-risk programs (e.g., NIH Pioneer awards) at small scale without changing the core system. Scaling what works in pilot high-risk programs to the core funding system is the unresolved challenge.

sources.title: Evidence and the Design and Reform of Scientific Institutions (Nintil)
